static_traits.name: Wang Kexin
static_traits.social_status: The relationship with her husband is affected by negative thoughts about food and body image; has a few close friends to confide in, but feels uneasy sharing these thoughts with friends
static_traits.medical_history: never experienced similar psychological problems; never received psychotherapy;No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Marked Self-deprecation (e.g. calling herself 'fat pig'), strict 'should' and self-discipline rules, tendency toward catastrophizing and overgeneralization, negating the positive, cooperative but skeptical in expression, Low mood and Strong guilt

basic_info.main_problem: After the husband prepared a surprise dinner containing butter for her, eating it produced strong guilt and self-loathing, and negative thoughts about body image and self-worth appeared, in turn affecting self-esteem and mood.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizes that negative thoughts about food and the body are affecting her mental health and her relationship with her husband, so seeks counseling to change these thinking patterns.

core_beliefs: My self-worth depends on whether I strictly control my diet and weight
Once I indulge in food, it proves I am a failure

special_situations.event: Husband prepares a surprise dinner and mentions using butter
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I eat high-fat food, it will ruin all my health efforts, showing I lack self-discipline
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Harsh self-criticism afterward, attempts to correct with positive self-talk, and plans to 'compensate' through a stricter diet
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am ruining my diet plan; one mistake will ruin everything; I am a 'fat pig'

special_situations.event: After eating 'indulgent' foods or a lavish meal
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should not eat certain foods; if I am not disciplined enough, it equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Making stricter diet rules, engaging in self-reproach and negation After meals
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not disciplined enough, I failed

special_situations.event: Special occasions or when the husband does something thoughtful (such as a surprise dinner)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not strictly refuse high-calorie foods at these moments, I will lose control and gain weight, and remain dissatisfied with my body for a long time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids enjoying the present, focuses on food ingredients and calories, persistently blames herself afterward
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This will ruin my health, I will keep gaining weight, and never be satisfied with my body again

special_situations.event: When enjoying a meal thoughtfully prepared by the partner
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Enjoying others' kindness is equated with indulging oneself and will weaken self-discipline
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive experiences, focusing only on unhealthy ingredients and potential consequences
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is not a good thing, I should not enjoy this meal

core_conflict.wish: Hopes to enjoy intimacy and care with her husband with peace of mind, and to keep moderation and confidence in diet
core_conflict.fear: Fearing losing control and gaining weight, becoming dissatisfied with my body and self-worth, thus being seen as a failure and affecting the intimate relationship
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of safety through harsh self-control and self-criticism, avoiding being seen as a 'failure'

object_relations.self_representation: The self prone to losing control and needing strict restraint
object_relations.object_representation: Others (e.g. the husband) who bring temptation and risk with good intentions

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When triggered by others' care or intimate gestures (e.g. the husband's surprise dinner), or when the counselor invites her to accept positive experiences and self-reward
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting care as a 'test' of self-discipline; once the strict standards are not met, seeing herself as a failure who needs punishment (transference: experiencing external goodwill as a potential threat)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use a strong self-reproach tone, frequently use 'I should not.../I failed', ignoring or minimizing others' goodwill and positive feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When facing guilt after eating and worries about weight
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: By emphasizing reasons such as 'one indulgence will ruin everything', finds justification for continued strict control and self-blame
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a rationalizing tone emphasizes rules and consequences (such as calories, weight gain), using 'therefore I must be stricter' to consolidate self-punishment and control.

manifestations: Constrains one's own diet and behavior with strict 'should/must' rules
Binds eating to self-worth, worries that once relaxed, control will be lost
Unable to freely enjoy others' care in intimate moments
outcomes: Difficulty enjoying intimate moments with husband

manifestations: Feeling uneasy sharing these troubles with friends
Negative thinking affecting interactions and intimacy with the husband
outcomes: Relationship tension and Increased sense of alienation
In eating-related situations, more inclined toward self-isolation and self-criticism

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using statements like 'I should not eat certain things', 'I must be more disciplined'
Taking external standards of health and weight directly as the criteria for self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Engaging in intense self-criticism and negation After meals
Worrying about not seeing immediate results and further blaming herself
Overly cautious in intimate moments; hard to allow enjoyment and relaxation

positive_force: Strong health awareness, values diet and body management
Able to identify and describe negative automatic thoughts, willing to try recording and reminder strategies
Has a certain amount of social support (several friends to confide in)
Open to change (although doubtful), willing to cooperate with the counselor
negative_force: Strict 'should' rules and black-and-white rules lead to self-blame
Catastrophizing and overgeneralization (one indulgence ruins everything)
Negating positive experiences, ignoring the partner's care and present enjoyment
Strong guilt and self-devaluation after eating, persistently affects mood and self-esteem
Worrying about losing control and gaining weight, excessively tying body image to self-worth

target_behavior.behavior: After eating, strong guilt and self-deprecation appear (such as calling themselves a 'fat pig'), accompanied by persistent negative rumination
antecedent: Eating foods seen as 'indulgent' or high-fat ingredients (such as butter)
Special occasions or lavish meals prepared by partner
After meals, reflects and compares whether the diet met strict rules
target_behavior.core_reason: Regards weight and dietary discipline as the core of self-worth, interpreting one indulgence as 'complete failure' through catastrophizing and all-or-nothing cognition, and seeks a sense of control through self-criticism
target_behavior.function: Avoidance (negative Reinforcement): temporarily relieving Anxiety about losing control and gaining weight through self-reproach and stricter rules, and trying to recover a sense of control; while also avoiding enjoyment and intimate experiences
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and Impaired self-esteem, unable to enjoy intimate moments with the partner, relationship affected; using After meals for ongoing pressure and negative rumination
